title: Aspirin, Butalbital, and Caffeine
overview: This combination of drugs is used to relieve tension headaches.

sections.Before taking aspirin, butalbital, and c: tell your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to aspirin, butalbital, caffeine, other pain relievers such as ibuprofen (Motrin), or any other drugs.tell your doctor and pharmacist what prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking while taking aspirin, butalbital, and caffeine. Your doctor may need to change the doses of your medications or monitor you carefully for side effects..The following nonprescription products may interact with aspirin, butalbital, and caffeine: medications for allergy (diphenhydramine, loratadine, fexofenadine, chlorpheniramine or cetirizine), nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)[ ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin, others), naproxen (Aleve, Naprosyn, others)], multivitamins, and medications for sleep. Be sure to let your doctor and pharmacist know that you are taking these medications before you start taking aspirin, butalbital, and caffeine. Do not start any of these medications while taking aspirin, butalbital, and caffeine without discussing with your healthcare provider.tell your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney disease, porphyria, bleeding problems, nasal polyps, ulcers, or a history of depression.tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant; or are breast-feeding. Aspirin may harm the fetus and cause problems with delivery if it is taken around 20 weeks or later during pregnancy. Do not take aspirin, butalbital, and caffeine around or after 20 weeks of pregnancy, unless you are told to do so by your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking aspirin, butalbital, and caffeine, call your doctor.you should know that this drug may make you drowsy. Do not drive a car or operate machinery until you know how this drug affects you.remember that alcohol can add to the drowsiness caused by this drug.
sections.If you experience any of the following s: skin rashitchingdifficulty breathingringing in the earsbloody or black stoolsIf you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may send a report to the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online (https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch) or by phone (1-800-332-1088).
